facts.claim: A lookup for a key that is already held returns the held instance; the new caller's factory is not run.
facts.catch_criteria: States that an immediate reopen gets the same instance and the passed factory is skipped.

facts.claim: The conversation-tree family holds at most 8 entries; inserting past the bound evicts the least recently used key that no owner pins.
facts.catch_criteria: States the bound of 8 conversation trees and least-recently-used eviction of unpinned keys.

facts.claim: Conversation trees are not pinned, so the first open is evicted after eight other opens; pins exist for other families such as subagent child measures.
facts.catch_criteria: States that conversation trees take no pin (unlike some other families), so eviction applies to them.

facts.claim: After eviction, the next lookup builds a new instance that folds the aggregate again from its start; eviction drops only the registry's reference.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the reopen after eight others refolds the history from the start.

facts.claim: A holder that kept the evicted instance keeps feeding and reading it, so two instances of one key can be live at once and the aggregate is folded twice.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the old holder keeps its own (evicted) instance, so two live instances of the same key can exist.

facts.claim: A holder must read through replay: getState returns only the last folded state, not a fresh read.
facts.catch_criteria: Distinguishes replay (fresh fold) from getState (last folded state).

facts.claim: Releasing a conversation tree drops only the registry reference: a holder keeps its instance, and the next ask builds a new one.
facts.catch_criteria: States that release (or eviction) does not close a holder's instance; it only makes the next ask build anew.

traps.wrong_answer: Held projections stay cached for the whole app session, so the reopen after eight others returns the same tree without rereading history.
Every open builds the tree from the factory it passes, so an immediate reopen with another factory yields a different tree.
The holder of the first open sees the reopened tree's state, because the registry always shares one instance per key.
